title.exam: FIFTH SEMESTER (CUFYUGP) DEGREE EXAMINATION: MODEL PAPER 1
title.subject: MATHEMATICS
title.module: Module I: Binary Operations and Isomorphic Binary Structures

sections.name: Section A
sections.rule: All Questions can be answered. Each Question carries 3 marks (Ceiling: 24 Marks)
questions: Let $\ast$ be defined on $\mathbb{Q}$ by $a \ast b = a/b$. Does $\ast$ define a binary operation on $\mathbb{Q}$? Justify your answer.
Show that the set of all odd integers is not closed under ordinary addition.
Let $\ast$ be defined on $\mathbb{Z}$ by $a \ast b = \max\{a, b\}$. Show that $\ast$ is commutative and associative.
Let $\ast$ be defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by $a \ast b = \dfrac{a+b}{2}$. Is $\ast$ commutative? Is it associative?
Let $S$ be a set with more than one element and let $a \ast b = a$ for all $a, b \in S$. Show that $\ast$ is associative but not commutative.
Give an example of a set with a binary operation which is commutative but not associative.
Show that the identity element of a set with a binary operation, if it exists, is unique.
Let $\ast$ be defined on $\mathbb{Z}$ by $a \ast b = a + b + 1$. Find the identity element of $\langle \mathbb{Z}, \ast \rangle$, if it exists.
State the condition that a function $f : \langle S, \ast \rangle \to \langle S', \circ \rangle$ must satisfy to be an isomorphism of binary structures.
Show that the binary structures $\langle \{0, 1\}, \ast \rangle$ with $a \ast b = a$, and $\langle \{0, 1\}, \circ \rangle$ with $a \circ b = \max\{a, b\}$, are not isomorphic.

sections.name: Section B
sections.rule: All Questions can be answered. Each Question carries 6 marks (Ceiling: 36 Marks)
questions: Let $\ast$ be defined on $\mathbb{Z}^+$ by $a \ast b = \min\{a, b\}$. Is $\ast$ a binary operation on $\mathbb{Z}^+$? Is it commutative? Justify your answer.
Show that $f : \mathbb{Z} \to 3\mathbb{Z}$ given by $f(m) = 3m$ is an isomorphism from $\langle \mathbb{Z}, + \rangle$ onto $\langle 3\mathbb{Z}, + \rangle$.

Show that the binary structure $\langle \mathbb{R}, + \rangle$ with operation the usual addition is isomorphic to the structure $\langle \mathbb{R}^+, \cdot \rangle$ where $\cdot$ is the usual multiplication.

Consider the following two binary structures: (a) $\mathbb{Z}$, the set of integers with ordinary addition; and (b) $2\mathbb{Z} = \{2n \mid n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$, the set of even integers with ordinary addition. Show that the above two binary structures are isomorphic.
Let $f : \langle S, \ast \rangle \to \langle S', \circ \rangle$ be an isomorphism of binary structures. Show that $f^{-1} : S' \to S$ is also an isomorphism of binary structures.
Let $f : \langle S, \ast \rangle \to \langle S', \circ \rangle$ be an isomorphism of binary structures. Show that if $\ast$ is commutative, then $\circ$ is commutative.
Show that the relation ‘$\langle S, \ast \rangle$ is isomorphic to $\langle S', \circ \rangle$’ is an equivalence relation on binary structures.
Let $\ast$ be defined on $\mathbb{Z}$ by $a \ast b = a + b + 1$. Show that $\langle \mathbb{Z}, \ast \rangle$ is isomorphic to $\langle \mathbb{Z}, + \rangle$.

sections.name: Section C
sections.rule: Answer any ONE. Each Question carries 10 marks (1x10=10 Marks)
questions: Let $\ast$ be defined on $\mathbb{R}$ by $a \ast b = a + b - ab$. (a) Show that $\ast$ is a binary operation on $\mathbb{R}$. (b) Show that $\ast$ is commutative and associative. (c) Find the identity element of $\langle \mathbb{R}, \ast \rangle$ and show that it is unique.
Show that the binary structures $\langle \mathbb{R}, + \rangle$ and $\langle \mathbb{R}, \cdot \rangle$ are not isomorphic.
